title: tcgen05 and TMEM: fifth-generation Tensor Core GEMM

steps.title: A single 128×128×64 tile: TMA → tcgen05.mma → TMEM → C
Full K loop: multi-stage TMA/mbarrier pipeline

cases.name: one_tile
cases.purpose: Exactly one tile and one K tile (4 MMAs): any mistake in the descriptor, the instruction descriptor or the TMEM row/column mapping makes the result not exactly equal.

cases.name: small
cases.purpose: Less than one tile in all three dimensions: TMA fills out-of-bounds elements with zero, expect_tx is still the byte count of the whole box; the write-back must clip out-of-bounds rows and columns.

cases.name: long_k
cases.purpose: A single tile, 16 K tiles: the ring buffer wraps around 4 times; a wrong full/empty parity or refill timing reads stale data.

cases.name: short_k
cases.purpose: 3 K tiles, fewer than the pipeline stages: the prologue must not load tiles that do not exist, and the last tile has only 8 valid columns.

cases.name: aligned
cases.purpose: Multiple CTAs, exact multiples of the tile: checks the mapping from blockIdx to (m0, n0) and the TMA coordinate order (x = k, y = row).

cases.name: tail
cases.purpose: Neither M nor N is a multiple of the tile: the second row of CTAs has only 5 valid rows, and the TMA store must clip the other rows.

cases.name: raster
cases.purpose: 11 × 3 CTAs (with BN = 256 the last column of CTAs has only 88 columns), a K tail of 8 columns.

cases.name: random
cases.purpose: Medium-size random data: error of the same order as cuBLAS.

cases.name: square
cases.purpose: Tensor Core throughput: 137 GFLOP, directly comparable with lab 21.

cases.name: wide
cases.purpose: 550 GFLOP, 128 MB of A and B together: more tiles, so the wave tail matters less.
